problem: Improve robot policies using pretrained visual world-model rollouts from images/instructions, and determine which gains survive real robot evaluation.
contribution: World-Gymnast applies model-based GRPO with VLM rewards, scene/instruction augmentation, test-time training and optional Dyna-style feedback. It explicitly evaluates on AutoEval physical tasks in addition to WorldGym predictions.
algorithm: Modified OpenVLA-OFT token-action policy alternates action chunks with600M WorldGym future frames. GPT4o assigns binary rollout reward; group-relative clipped updates omitKL, resample zero-variance groups and increase exploration temperature. Image editing adds distractors, language prompts add tasks, and actual rollout data may refit the world model between policy rounds.
observations: Initial RGB and language, recent generated images; proprioception/secondary cameras removed. Training from 'any frame' means frames sufficiently near world-model support, not arbitrary scenes. Generated rewards can hallucinate.
actions: Five-action chunks via LLaMA2 language-model head instead of default L1 head. Assumes Bridge/WidowX action convention; no direct target-arm retargeting component is provided.
embodiment_and_data: BridgeDataV2/WidowX policy with OXE-pretrained WorldGym;17 curated evaluation tasks. Actual AutoEval covers4tasks/2setups with10trials repeated5times. Full policy training4 H200140GB GPUs1–2days. Dyna extension collects~100actual trajectories/task and120kmodel-finetuning steps.
experiments: Compare SFT, equal synthesized-rollout Iter-SFT, and SIMPLER-RL including digital twins. Diverse augmentation results Table3 are WorldGym evaluation, not all physical. Test-time close-drawer adaptation and iterative world-model updates are separate experiments from base held-out evaluation.
baselines: SFT and Iter-SFT; SIMPLER uses partial rewards to prevent all-failure groups and includes test-task digital twins, while model-based training uses broader scene data. Preserve these reward/data differences.
quantitative_result: Table1 PDFp5 physicalclose-drawer SIMPLER74±5% versusWorld-Gymnast62±6% negative result; eggplant-blue-sink32±10% versus72±10%. Table2 same task SFT4±4%,Iter-SFT10±3%,World-Gymnast72±10%. SE computed over five10-trialgroups. Table3p6 WorldGym-only augmentation74±3→81±1%language. Test-time close-drawer62±6→100±0%p7, with degradation on other tasks explicitly reported.
limitations: Far-OOD initial scenes unsupported; VLM rewards may hallucinate and policies exploit generated physics. Test-time adaptation overfits one task and harms others. High GPU requirement and model generation cost differ from embedded execution. WorldGym-estimated success is not physical validation; repeated online updates incur real collection cost.
code_and_license: Primary project world-gymnast.github.io; code/model/data license texts not independently inspected. WorldGym,OpenVLA,Bridge and external image/VLM services require separate provenance/rights. No code inspected/executed.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE offline model-ranking and limited simulation policy updates; prefer the paper's distinction between predicted and actual outcomes. NX16GB training parity and new SO101 morphology are unsupported. Any target model requires calibrated target action semantics and fresh observed validation, preserving existing controller settings.
